answer: Because the dune stake is held until the comet settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the basalt audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 47% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one. A farm running 102 keys hence pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
